We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available precursors). The target is COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This looks like a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1,4-dione?). Actually structure: a bicyclic (decalin) with two carbonyls (one ketone, one ester). The SMILES: COC(=O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O? Wait given: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. That's methyl ester of a bicyclic acid? The core is a bicyclic di-ketone (maybe 1,4-naphthoquinone?). Let's decode: COC(=O) attached to chiral carbon bridging two rings, which also has a ketone on the other side. So it's methyl 2-oxodecahydro-naphthalene-1-carboxylate? Anyway.

Goal: find commercially available chemicals that can directly give this via a single reaction. Likely esterification of a carboxylic acid with methanol (or methylation). So precursor could be the corresponding carboxylic acid: O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O (the acid). Is that commercially available? We checked is_buyable: false.

Alternative: start from methyl 2-oxodecahydro-naphthalene-1-carboxylate? That's the target itself. Not helpful.

Maybe we can use a protected form: methyl 2-oxodecahydro-naphthalene-1-carboxylate can be formed via oxidation of methyl decalin? Not.

We need a single-step reaction from available chemicals. Could be transesterification from ethyl ester? Ethyl ester of same acid maybe available. Check ethyl ester: CCOC(=O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O. Check buyable.
